description_full: OSI Systems, Inc. designs and manufactures specialized electronic systems and components for critical applications in the United States, Mexico, the rest of Americas, the United Kingdom, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia-Pacific. The company offers security products, such as baggage and parcel inspection, cargo and vehicle inspection, hold baggage screening, people screening, radiation monitoring, explosive and narcotics trace detection, and optical inspection systems; turnkey security screening services for enterprise inspection process integration, operator training, and the staffing and operation of security screening checkpoints under the S2 brand. It also provides trace detection systems for trace amounts of explosives and narcotics and people screening products, including walk-through metal detectors for use at security checkpoints at airports, government buildings, sports arenas, and other venues; digital and analog high-power RF systems; and active components for detection of lights of different wavelengths and converts light into electrical signals. In addition, the company offers devices for emitting light in the form of lasers; passive components for amplifying, separating, and reflecting light under the OSI Optoelectronics brand; and printed circuit board assemblies, cable and harness assemblies, and complete systems. Further, it provides bedside monitors, such as the Xprezzon and Qube, as well as telemetry solutions; Spacelabs SafeNSound for assisting hospitals; predictive analytics clinical decision support solutions; Pathfinder SL and Lifescreen Pro analysis tools; and Eclipse Pro Holter recorders. Additionally, the company offers Eclipse Mini Ambulatory ECG recorders; ambulatory blood pressure monitors; Spacelabs OnTrak ambulatory blood pressure systems; Sentinel, a cardiology information management system; and multivendor compatible accessories. OSI Systems, Inc. was incorporated in 1987 and is headquartered in Hawthorne, California.

financial_summary: OSI Systems, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $3.0B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 8% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 34%.

The business throws off $245M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.78× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.5× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 8.3×.
Management returns a meaningful 9.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.7% of the shares.

sect: Its 12% operating margin runs 5pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.52x).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-5.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 29% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 38% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 41% and a beta of 1.06, it moves roughly with the market.
About $40.1M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 47% in the 2020 crash, 31% in the 2022 bear market and 59% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 34% below its DCF fair value of $294, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 13%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $180 to $477 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 20.7 vs 27.4 and P/FCF 12.4 vs 26.1 (sector median).
The EBIT multiple is close to its own 10-year median (-5%).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 8.1% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The 7 covering analysts target $273 on average, 42% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 8.4%, but the 5pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.33).
It runs a 34% gross margin and converts 14% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.78x.
ROE of 19% is amplified by 3.0x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
It spends 4.4% of revenue on R&D and 1.5% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.5x net debt to EBITDA ($359.8M of cash against $1.0B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 8.3x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.1, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 232 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 11.8% over 3 years, 9.3% over 5 years and 8.0% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 13.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 14.8% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.54 (orders lagging sales), a backlog worth 0% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 16%.
Capex runs only 0.7x depreciation (1.7% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 22, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 4.7%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 9.0% a year to shareholders (9.0% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 2.3% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 22.1% of the float, 9.7 days to cover.
people: With about 7,806 employees, each generates about $229K of revenue, 0.6x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 6.0% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $31K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.5M (11x revenue per employee).
